subject: Request: EU failover RTO exception for Horizon Pay
messages:
From: Olivia Morton <olivia.morton@horizonpay.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts@horizonpay.com
Date: 2027-03-14T14:12:00+01:00
Subject: EU failover RTO - request for carve-out

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. As we prepare procurement and our security review, a couple of EU-specific constraints came up that affect our multi-region failover posture. We operate with strict data residency and replication rules for certain European merchant data; the current default Redwood SLA (15m RTO for regional failover) requires cross-region KV sync and warm standby that would cause us to move controlled data outside our approved boundaries during a failover runbook.

We would like to request a formal exception to allow a 30-minute RTO for EU-regulated traffic (rather than 15 minutes), combined with the following compensating controls:
- Documented runbook showing permitted steps for read-only failover first, then phased write cutover.
- Additional audit logging for all failover events.
- Quarterly tabletop exercises witnessed by Horizon Pay security.

We've attached a short note outlining the constraints (horizonpay-initial-ask.pdf). Procurement is also asking for an updated SLA amendment they can route to legal. Can Redwood provide a proposed amendment and any technical mitigations you can commit to?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we are aiming to sign by end of month.

Best,
Olivia Morton
Head of Infrastructure & Security
Horizon Pay

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Morton <olivia.morton@horizonpay.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T16:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: EU failover RTO - request for carve-out

Olivia — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment.

We can absolutely take this through our internal SLA exceptions flow. I’ve looped Rishi (engineering) and Marissa (sales/procurement) so we can draft a concrete amendment that maps the compensating controls to technical commitments.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Rishi will propose an operational amendment (target: 30m RTO for the defined EU-regulated traffic) and outline mitigations.
- Marissa will prepare a redline-friendly PDF we can send to your procurement/legal.
- We’ll propose quarterly tabletop cadence and include additional audit log retention for failover events.

Can you confirm the scope — is this limited to EU-regulated merchant PII and transaction metadata (yes/no)? Also please confirm any specific countries with additional restrictions (e.g., AT/DE/FR).

I’ll aim to have a draft over by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: horizonpay-initial-ask.pdf

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T17:30:00+01:00
Subject: RE: EU failover RTO - request for carve-out

Lauren / Marissa — notes from infra after a quick review: we can support a scoped 30-minute RTO for Horizon Pay EU-regulated traffic under the following operational constraints (technical summary):

1) Scope definition: We treat the "EU-regulated traffic" as a taggable routing policy in our Smart Routing layer. Horizon must define the dataset CIDR and logical IDs that fall under this scope.

2) Failover approach: Implement a staged failover: (a) DNS-prefetch & read-only routing to warm replicas within the EU primary region (no cross-border writes), (b) controlled KV state sync with scoped encryption key policies, (c) staged write cutover up to the 30m RTO target. This avoids unsanctioned data egress during the initial 0-15m window.

3) Compensating controls: extra audit log stream (retained 1 year), Doc-level immutability marker for any records involved in failover, and mandatory tabletop drills every quarter (we can host and provide a post-drill report).

4) Service implications: During the 16-30m window we expect degraded latency for write-heavy workflows; we will provide an SLA credit mechanism for failed availability beyond 30m tied to the amended SLA.

5) Operational commitments: Redwood will add a runbook appendix to the SLA amendment, provide a signed attestation for audit teams, and offer a 30-day warm standby validation test pre-signing.

I drafted language that Marissa can shape into the formal amendment. Also attaching an internal diagram to show the staged approach.

--Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: network-architecture-diagram.png

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Morton <olivia.morton@horizonpay.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T09:22:00+01:00
Subject: Proposed amendment: EU failover RTO exception (Horizon Pay)

Hi Olivia — attaching a draft amendment that implements Rishi’s operational constraints and the compensating controls we discussed (proposed-sla-amendment.pdf).

Summary of what’s in the draft: 
- Formal carve-out: 30-minute RTO for defined EU-regulated dataset (scope table included).
- Staged failover runbook (Appendix A) and required quarterly tabletop exercises.
- Audit log retention and an attestation clause for failover events.
- SLA credit schedule for unplanned outages exceeding the 30-minute window.
- 30-day warm-standby validation period to be executed before go-live.

Action items for Horizon Pay to expedite:
1) Confirm scope table (list of services/data types/countries) — I included a placeholder where you can list specific PII classes.
2) Sign via DocuSign (link below) or propose redlines.

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC123-horizonpay-sla

If it helps, we can also schedule a 30-minute call with Rishi tomorrow morning to walk the runbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-sla-amendment.pdf

From: Olivia Morton <olivia.morton@horizonpay.com>

Subject: Re: Proposed amendment: EU failover RTO exception (Horizon Pay)

Marissa — thank you. We reviewed the draft with legal and security this morning. The amendment language looks good; we only made two minor edits to the scope table (added AT and removed a deprecated dataset ID).

We will sign via DocuSign today and start scheduling the warm-standby validation (can we target March 28 for the first run?). I’ll send a quick calendar invite for the validation planning call.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — this clears the path for our procurement team to close the contract.

Best,
Olivia Morton
Head of Infrastructure & Security
Horizon Pay
